# App Shell

**Figma:** ◇ Master-Layout AppShell patterns (16254:1057): Pattern/AppShell/Desktop (16258:1857), Pattern/AppShell/Mobile (16261:136204), Header/AppShell (16243:290461), .Primitives/AppShell/Pane (16254:1099), Action-Bar/Mobile (16326:6489); Header/Action-Item (12280:19532) + Notification-Dot (4116:21789)  
**Import:** `import { AppShell, AppShellHeader, AppShellPane, AppShellAction, AppShellAccount, useAppShell } from "@zen-ds/react";`

The frame of an app, built on Figma's AppShell patterns. From 1024px (desktops, iPad landscape) a desktop pattern: Sidebar · List-Detail · Top-Bar · Workspace · Docs · Focus · Grid, with Header/AppShell, panes, progress, a docked side panel and floating actions. Narrower, with mobile parts (phones, iPad portrait), a mobile pattern: the TopNavigation as a Bar, a Band with a hero, a Band-Sheet or over Media, then the Tab-Bar, a floating glass bar or an Action bar. Without mobile parts a narrow shell keeps its header and opens the Sidebar as a modal drawer. The Body pads Margin-Comfortable, so the page needs no Container for the margins.

## Use it for
- Every app screen: one AppShell at the root, inside ZenProvider.
- Navigation between a few roots → pattern="sidebar" (the default); a list beside its detail (inbox, requests) → "list-detail"; one company or product without navigation → "top-bar"; tools around a canvas → "workspace"; reading → "docs"; one task with steps → "focus"; the Sidebar workspace drawn in lines (dense dashboards, analytics, admin) → "grid".
- A phone or an upright iPad → topNavigation with bottomNavigation (roots) or actionBar (a task's actions); a brand band → mobileTop="band" with hero; a profile or a summary rising over colour → "band-sheet"; a photo, video or map → "media" with backdrop.
- Header icon actions with an unread dot or count → AppShellAction; the account menu → Menu with an AppShellAccount trigger.

## Use something else for
- Marketing pages → Container + your own header.
- A modal flow → Dialog or SidePanel type="modal".
- Page actions (Submit, Export, New) → the PageHeader actions in the header's main, not its top row.
- A second shell inside a pane or a card → one AppShell per screen.

### AppShell
The frame of an app, built on Figma's AppShell patterns (◇ Master-Layout 16254:1057): Pattern/AppShell/Desktop (16258:1857) from 1024px, Pattern/AppShell/Mobile (16261:136204) below it when a mobile part is given, with a "Skip to content" link, a modal navigation drawer and a docked or modal side panel. Desktop (`pattern`): Sidebar, Header/AppShell (`header`, an AppShellHeader), the Body (`children`, padded Margin-Comfortable), the panes (`leadingPane`, `trailingPane`, AppShellPane), `progress`, `sidePanel` and `floatingActions`. Mobile (`mobileTop`): the TopNavigation, the band's `hero` or the `backdrop`, the Body, then the `bottomNavigation` or the `actionBar`. The Sidebar, the header, the panes and the bars stay in view while the page scrolls (the window or the frame around the shell). <AppShell sidebar={<Sidebar … />} header={<AppShellHeader leading={<Breadcrumbs … />} actions={…} main={<PageHeader … />} />}> …the page… `</AppShell>`

Also accepts `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "children">`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pattern` | `"sidebar" \| "list-detail" \| "top-bar" \| "workspace" \| "docs" \| "focus" \| "grid"` | `"sidebar"` | Figma Layout, the desktop structure (from 1024px: desktops and iPad landscape): - `sidebar` (default): Sidebar · header + page · docked side panel. - `list-detail`: the Sidebar's rail · `leadingPane` (a 360 list) · header + the selected item. - `top-bar`: no Sidebar; the header across, its sections or centre holding the navigation. - `workspace`: the header across the top · `leadingPane` · page · `trailingPane` (tools, properties). - `docs`: as workspace, the page a centred 720 column for reading, the panes on the Canvas. - `focus`: one task: the header across · `progress` · a 680 column with the `trailingPane` (a summary) beside it. - `grid`: as `sidebar`, drawn in lines instead of surfaces (Layout=Grid, 16258:1857): the Sidebar takes Theme=Border, Density=Small (no fill, a Pale line on its inner edge) and the header Theme=Border & Divider, Density=Small (a Pale line under its top row), unless they set their own `theme` / `density`. ### AppShellHeader
Figma Header/AppShell (16783:71068; Theme=Default 16243:290461), the header of Pattern/AppShell/Desktop. The Main frame pads Margin-Comfortable above (Margin-Compact at Density=Small) and at the sides and Spacing/Padding/Small below, Spacing/Gap/Large between its rows (`theme="border-divider"` pads each row itself, a Pale line under the top row): - Top-Header: the Sidebar's collapse toggle (Collapse Button: a Button/Icon-Flat Small Primary in a 20px wrapper, while the AppShell has `collapse="header"`) or, on a narrow shell, the menu button that opens the navigation drawer; then Top-Elements: `leading` · `center` · `actions` (Primitives/Dashboard/Header Type=Navigation), Spacing/Gap/Medium apart. - Main-Element: `main`, the page's own header. Under the Main frame, Sections: `sections`. Pass it as the AppShell's `header`; on a phone the shell shows its `topNavigation` instead.

Also accepts `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, "children">`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `leading` | `ReactNode` | — | Figma Top-Elements › Leading-Slots: where the user is, usually `<Breadcrumbs size="sm">`, or a Search. It grows. |
| `center` | `ReactNode` | — | Figma Center-Slots: the row's middle, up to 400px and centred between `leading` and `actions`, e.g. a Search. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | — | Figma Trailing-Slots, Spacing/Gap/Small apart: a plan Badge, `AppShellAction` buttons (notifications, help), then the account (`<Menu trigger={<AppShellAccount … />}>`). Page actions belong in `main`. |
| `main` | `ReactNode` | — | Figma Main-Element (the Main row): the page's own header, usually `<PageHeader title=… />` with its actions. |
| `sections` | `ReactNode` | — | Figma Sections: rows under the Main row, e.g. `<Tabs>` for the page's views or a toolbar of Search + filters. |
| `theme` | `"default" \| "border-divider"` | — | Figma Theme: `default` (one Main frame: Margin-Comfortable above and at the sides, Padding/Small below, Spacing/Gap/Large between the rows) · `border-divider` (Theme=Border & Divider, 16783:72140: the top row pads Padding/Small · Margin-Comfortable with a 1px Border/Neutral/Pale line under it; the Main row pads Padding/Medium · Margin-Comfortable). Unset follows the AppShell: `pattern="grid"` draws border-divider, other patterns default. |
| `density` | `"medium" \| "small"` | — | Figma Density: `medium` (Margin-Comfortable above) · `small` (Margin-Compact above, 16823:76454). Unset follows the AppShell: `pattern="grid"` draws small, other patterns medium. The border-divider theme pads its rows itself. |
| `overrides` | `Readonly<Record<string, Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>>>` | — | Figma instance overrides, by layer (`{ Collapse: { level: "secondary" } }`). Written by Zen Studio. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` | — | The root `<header>` element. |

### AppShellPane
Figma .Primitives/AppShell/Pane (16254:1099): a side pane of Pattern/AppShell/Desktop (List-Detail's list, Workspace's and Docs' leading and trailing panes, Focus' summary). Corner-Radius/XLarge; Pane-Header pads Margin-Compact at the top and sides and Spacing/Padding/XSmall below, Spacing/Gap/XSmall between the title and the action; Pane-Content pads Spacing/Padding/XSmall with Spacing/Gap/XSmall between its rows. The AppShell sizes it (`leadingPane`, `trailingPane`).

Also accepts `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, "title" | "children">`.

| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4` | `2` | Heading level of the title. Default 2: a pane sits beside the page's h1. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` | — | Figma Action: one icon action at the end of the header, usually `<IconButton appearance="flat" level="secondary" size="sm" …>` (a 20px glyph with a 32px hit area). |

| `surface` | `"default" \| "alt"` | `"default"` | Figma Surface for the default and border themes: `default` Surface/Default · `alt` Surface/Alt. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | Figma Pane-Content: the pane's body (a List, a tree, filters, a summary). |

### AppShellAction
Figma Primitives/Dashboard/Header/Action-Item (12280:19532): a header icon action with an optional Primitives/Notification-Dot (4116:21789). Dot 8px, Number Badge/Size/2XSmall high with Label/Small/Medium text, both on Color/Background/{Negative|Positive|Accent}/Solid with a 2px Color/Border/Inverse ring, at the button's top-right. It forwards its ref and props to the button, so it can be a <Menu trigger>.

Also accepts `Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "children">`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` (required) | `IconName \| ReactNode` | — | Figma Leading-Icon: an icon name (`"icon-bell-01-line"`) or a node. |
| `aria-label` (required) | `string` | — | The action's name (“Notifications”): its accessible name, with the unread count added, and its 1s tooltip. |
| `count` | `number` | — | Figma Noti-type=Number: the unread count on a badge. 0 hides it; above 99 it reads "99+" (the accessible name keeps the exact number). |
| `dot` | `boolean` | `false` | Figma Noti-type=Dot: something new without a count. Hidden while a count shows. |
| `tone` | `"default" \| "active" \| "accent"` | `"default"` | Figma Notification-Dot Theme: `default` Negative (needs attention) · `active` Positive · `accent`. |
| `appearance` | `"tertiary" \| "flat"` | `"tertiary"` | Figma Theme: `tertiary` (Button/Icon-Main Medium Tertiary, 40px) · `flat` (Button/Icon-Flat Medium Primary: a 20px glyph with a 40px hit area). |
| `tooltip` | `ReactNode \| false` | — | Tooltip text. Default: `aria-label` (without the count). |
| `overrides` | `Readonly<Record<string, Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>>>` | — | Figma instance overrides: props of the icon button it draws, by layer (`{ Button: { level: "secondary" } }`). Written by Zen Studio; app code sets icon / appearance. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` | — | Ref to the icon button element, so the action can be a `<Menu trigger>`. |

### AppShellAccount
The account button at the end of the header's top row: Figma Avatar/Single Circle Medium (Image-Size/Medium) as a button. Put it in a Menu for the account actions: `<Menu align="end" trigger={<AppShellAccount name="Ava Chen" src={photo} />} items={…} />`. Keyboard focus shows the Avatar's own focus ring.

Also accepts `Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "children">`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (required) | `string` | — | The signed-in person's name: the accessible name (“Account: Ava Chen”), the tooltip and the initials without a photo. |
| `src` | `string` | — | Photo URL (Figma Avatar/Single Theme=Photo). |
| `theme` | `Exclude<AvatarTheme, "photo">` | `"neutral"` | Initials colour without a photo. Default neutral. |
| `overrides` | `Readonly<Record<string, Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>>>` | — | Figma instance overrides: props of the avatar it draws, by layer (`{ Avatar: { shape: "square" } }`). Written by Zen Studio; app code sets src / theme. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` | — | Ref to the account button element, so it can be a `<Menu trigger>`. |
| `type` | _HTML attribute_ | `"button"` |  |

## ✅ Do
- Put one AppShell at the root of each app screen, inside ZenProvider, and pick the pattern from the screen's job (see Use).
- With pattern="grid", build the page from Boxes and Flat Cards (MetricCard, ChartCard and Card keep theme flat) on the grey Canvas, and give Subtle only to a metric card that should stand out (◇ Master-Layout Rule, 16823:85229).
- One elevation per screen, set by the Sidebar: Canvas default (grey) + the default Sidebar (Surface + shadow) + Shadow cards and panes; Canvas alt (white) + a Surface-alt or Flat Sidebar + bordered cards and panes (theme="border"); Canvas flat + a Flat Sidebar + bordered cards. Never a shadowed Sidebar on a white Canvas.
- Lead the header's top row with Breadcrumbs (master={false} beside the toggle) or a Search, and keep its right side to utilities in this order: a plan Badge, AppShellAction buttons, the account menu last.
- Put the page's PageHeader in the header's main (one h1) and its views (Tabs) in sections; the Body holds the content at the page margin, with no Container.
- Give both side panes the same width (workspace and docs size them for you) and one theme.
- Show unread items on the action itself (AppShellAction count or dot) so the count is also in its accessible name.
- Store the rail state from onSidebarCollapsedChange so the Sidebar opens the way people left it.
- For an app that runs on phones, give the shell its mobile parts mapped from the header: Sidebar rows → BottomNavigation (up to 5; more → the first 4 + More), Breadcrumbs → Back on a child screen, the PageHeader title → the TopNavigation title (large on a root), at most 3 trailing actions, the account → the avatar on a root (component-usage-rules §17).

## ❌ Don't
- Don't build your own sidebar + main flex layout, your own panes or your own drawer.
- Don't put primary page actions in the header's top row (harness: app-shell/primary-in-top-bar).
- Don't put a Master crumb right after the header's collapse toggle: master={false}, or collapse="sidebar" (harness: app-shell/collapse-beside-master-crumb).
- Don't give a pattern a part it does not draw, such as a trailingPane on sidebar (harness: app-shell/pattern-parts).
- Don't nest AppShells (harness: app-shell/nested).
- Don't repeat the Breadcrumbs in the PageHeader when the top row shows them (harness: app-shell/breadcrumbs-once).
- Don't force layout in an app (harness: app-shell/forced-layout).
- Don't put the PageHeader in the Body when the shell has a topNavigation: on a phone it stays beside the bar's title, two h1s (harness: app-shell/page-header-in-main).
- Don't give the phone bar other words than the PageHeader title (harness: app-shell/top-navigation-title).

## Accessibility
- The first Tab stop is a "Skip to content" link: it moves focus to `<main>` (tabindex=-1) without touching the URL, so hash routers keep working.
- The drawer is a modal dialog named after navLabel: focus moves to the current page's row, Tab stays inside, the page behind is inert, and Close, Escape or the scrim close it with focus back on the menu button. Picking a page closes it and moves focus to `<main>`.
- The collapse toggle has aria-expanded and aria-controls, and names its action (Collapse sidebar / Expand sidebar) in a 1s tooltip; in the Sidebar's header it keeps the same name.
- Each pane is a region named by its title (an h2 by default, headingLevel to change it).
- An AppShellAction reads its unread count ("Notifications, 12 new"); the badge itself is hidden from assistive tech.
- The account button is named "Account: `<name>`" and shows the Avatar's focus ring.

## Content
- Breadcrumbs name places in sentence case ("Time off"), the last one being the current page.
- Pane titles are nouns ("Files", "Comments · 3"); action names are nouns for places (Notifications, Settings, Help); the count is added automatically.

## Harness (`npm run usage:check`)
| Rule | Severity | Checks | Suppress with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon-button/needs-action` | warn | An IconButton (and AppShell's top-bar AppShellAction / AppShellAccount) does something: it has onClick (or href, or type="submit"), unless it is a Menu trigger (the Menu wires it). | `zen-allow-no-action: <reason>` |
| `app-shell/primary-in-top-bar` | warn | With a Main row, the header's top row (leading, center, actions) holds utilities: Breadcrumbs or a Search, a plan Badge, AppShellAction buttons and the account menu; a Primary or Accent page action belongs in the Main row's PageHeader actions. A header without a Main row (Figma Top-Bar, Workspace, Docs) keeps its product's Primary in the top row. | `zen-allow-top-bar-primary: <reason>` |
| `app-shell/nested` | error | One AppShell per screen: a shell inside another shell repeats the navigation, the header and <main>. | `zen-allow-nested-shell: <reason>` |
| `app-shell/breadcrumbs-once` | warn | Breadcrumbs appear once: in the header's top row (leading) or in the Main row's PageHeader, never both. | `zen-allow-breadcrumbs-twice: <reason>` |
| `app-shell/forced-layout` | warn | An app lets AppShell pick its layout from its own width (auto: the desktop pattern from 1024px; narrower the mobile pattern when it has mobile parts, else the drawer); layout="desktop", "drawer" or "mobile" is for previews and tests. (App mode only.) | `zen-allow-forced-layout: <reason>` |
| `app-shell/page-header-in-main` | warn | The page's PageHeader goes in the header's Main row (AppShellHeader main), not in the Body: with a topNavigation a phone shows the bar's title instead, and a PageHeader in the Body would stay beside it (two h1s, component-usage-rules §17). | `zen-allow-page-header-in-content: <reason>` |
| `app-shell/top-navigation-title` | warn | The phone bar (topNavigation's TopNavigation title) and the page header (the header's main PageHeader title) say the same words (component-usage-rules §17). | `zen-allow-phone-title: <reason>` |
| `app-shell/collapse-beside-master-crumb` | error | With the collapse toggle in the header (collapse="header", the default), the trail starts at a Sub level (Breadcrumbs master={false}): a Master crumb's home icon beside the toggle reads as two controls in a row. To keep the Master crumb, move the toggle into the Sidebar (collapse="sidebar"). (User rule 2026-10-18; Figma audit navigation/collapse-beside-master-crumb.) | `zen-allow-toggle-beside-master: <reason>` |
| `app-shell/pattern-parts` | warn | Each desktop pattern draws its own parts: leadingPane on list-detail, workspace and docs; trailingPane on workspace, docs and focus; progress on focus; the Sidebar beside the page on sidebar and list-detail. A part the pattern does not draw only shows on a narrow screen. | `zen-allow-pattern-parts: <reason>` |
| `api/overrides-studio-only` | error | `overrides` (Figma instance overrides of the layers a component draws itself: `{ "Sub-Action": { level: "danger" } }`) is written by Zen Studio on the pages it makes; hand-written code sets the component's own props or composes the parts (the user's call, 2026-10-10). | `zen-allow-overrides: <reason>` |
| `interaction/no-noop-handler` | warn | Every interaction a Zen control offers works: no no-op handlers (`() => {}`, `() => undefined`), which leave a field that ignores typing and ↑/↓ or a Dismiss that stays. Chat has chat/no-locked-interaction. | `zen-allow-noop-handler: <reason>` |
| `interaction/controlled-needs-handler` | warn | A controlled prop comes with its change handler (month + onMonthChange, value + onValueChange, open + onOpenChange, pageSize + onPageSizeChange…): without it nothing can change the value and the control is frozen, e.g. a DatePicker whose Previous/Next do nothing. Bare booleans (a fixed preview) and `x ? true : undefined` pins pass. | `zen-allow-controlled-handler: <reason>` |
